description: Recreates the structured-training-plan aesthetic of a running-coach app — an indigo-black dark-first canvas, a lime 'go' accent reserved for action, a fixed run-type color language, and the two signature components (the training-week strip and the guided-run session card) as paste-ready SwiftUI.

whatYouGet: A full SwiftUI color/type token file matching a structured-running-plan visual language (indigo + lime, dark-first canvas, fixed run-type palette)
The two signature components built out: a horizontal color-coded weekly plan strip and a gradient guided-run session card with a workout-structure breakdown
House rules that keep the run-type color coding, the lime-is-action-only discipline, and heavy tabular pace numerals consistent across every new screen you generate
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer who specializes in training and coaching apps for endurance athletes. You think in terms of at-a-glance scannability under fatigue: a runner should be able to read a whole week's plan, or a single workout's structure, in under two seconds.

</role>

<reference_data>
Color tokens (dark-first canvas, hex + role):
- Canvas #0E0E16 (blue-black tinted toward indigo, never neutral grey)
- Surface 1 #181826 (cards), Surface 2 #222234 (chips/segmented track), Divider #2C2C42
- Structural brand color: Indigo #4F46E5 (bright variant #6366F1, pressed #4338CA) — plan surfaces, today cell, session-card gradient, informational buttons
- Action/"go" brand color: Lime #C2F94E (pressed #A3D93B) — Start button, today-marker dot, primary CTAs, PR badges. Always paired with near-black text #1A1A1A, never used as text-on-dark
- Fixed run-type semantic palette: Easy/Recovery #34D399, Tempo/Threshold #FBBF24, Intervals/Speed #FB7185, Long Run #4F46E5
- Text: primary #F3F3FB, secondary #9C9CB8, tertiary #65657E
- Light-mode variants: canvas #F6F6FB, surface #FFFFFF, divider #E5E5F0

Typeface ladder: Sora (geometric sans, squared curves), heavy 700-800 on every numeral (pace, distance, splits), regular 400 on prose. Sizes: screen title 32/800, session title 21/800, section title 22/700, stat value 18/800, eyebrow 11/700 uppercase tracked +1.2pt in lime, pace/tag 12/700, tab label 10/600.

Corner radius scale: 8pt structure bar, 10pt run-type chips, 14pt cards/buttons/day-cells, 22pt the hero session card, 999pt pills.

Distinctive named patterns to reproduce:
1. Training-plan week strip — 7 equal-flex day cells, ~0.62 aspect ratio, 14pt radius, 7pt gaps; states are Completed (green-tinted bg/border), Today (solid indigo bg + lime dot + white text), Rest (muted tertiary text), Upcoming (run-type-colored dot).
2. Guided run-session card — 22pt-radius card, linear gradient #4F46E5 to a darker indigo (~150deg), a decorative translucent lime circle bleeding off the bottom-right corner, a lime pill tag, white session title, a 3-stat row, and a full-width lime CTA with a play glyph.
3. Workout-structure breakdown — a segmented horizontal bar (8pt radius, 3pt gaps) sized proportionally to phase duration, followed by per-step rows with a colored phase-code icon, title/description, and a right-aligned pace value with a small unit sublabel.
4. Run-type chip — small pill, run-type color fill, near-black text (white only on the indigo Long chip).

</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Lime never appears as body or label text on the dark canvas — it is a fill only, and any text sitting on a lime fill must be the near-black ink, never white or the default text color.
2. The run-type color mapping is fixed across the whole app (Easy/Tempo/Intervals/Long) — never recolor it per-screen or let a designer's mood palette override it, since athletes learn to read effort by color.
3. Every pace or numeric readout — splits, distance, duration, targets — uses heavy weight (700-800) and tabular/monospaced figures so a live run screen or a step list never jitters as digits change.
4. The weekly plan strip is placed directly beneath the screen header, never below the day's session card — it is the at-a-glance summary and must not be buried in scroll.
5. Cards are squared-soft (14-22pt radius), never fully rounded or pill-shaped — the geometry should read disciplined and athletic, not playful.
6. On the dark canvas, elevation comes from a surface-lift + hairline border, not drop shadows; the one exception is a soft indigo glow reserved for the hero session card, so it reads as the energized focal element.
7. Pace values in any step-by-step list are right-aligned in a consistent column so a runner's eye can scan targets vertically without re-reading labels.
8. Motion should feel purposeful and quick: staggered fade-ins for lists (~40ms per item), a one-shot subtle pulse on the "today" element, and smooth linear/eased growth for any bar or progress element — never bouncy or playful easing.
9. Any brand-accent interaction (start button, PR flag) should pair a scale-down press state with a haptic tap, reinforcing that these are the app's few high-stakes actions.

</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name / product: [e.g., a marathon-training companion]
- Primary athlete goal (5K / 10K / half / full / general fitness): [fill in]
- Screens needed (pick from: plan overview, single workout detail, live-run tracker, post-run summary, progress/trends, club/social feed): [list]
- Units preference (km or mi, or user-toggleable): [fill in]
- Any additional run types beyond Easy/Tempo/Intervals/Long (e.g., Fartlek, Hill repeats): [fill in or "none"]
- Light-mode support required?: [yes/no]
- Platform target (iPhone only / iPhone+iPad / +Watch companion): [fill in]
- Any brand-name substitutions for Indigo/Lime, if this isn't literally Runna: [fill in or "keep as-is"]

</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete SwiftUI Color and Font extension file implementing every token above, ready to paste into a project.
2. Full SwiftUI view code for the training-plan week strip component, including all four day-cell states and the entrance stagger animation.
3. Full SwiftUI view code for the guided run-session card, including the gradient, the decorative lime circle, the stat row, and the CTA button.
4. Full SwiftUI view code for the workout-structure breakdown (segmented bar + step rows).
5. A bottom tab bar implementation matching the icon/label/active-state spec.
6. A short written rationale (5-8 bullets) explaining how each of the listed screens in <the_project> should be composed from these components, in what order, and why.
7. A do/don't checklist (10 items) an engineer can use to sanity-check any new screen against this system before merging.

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer who specializes in wellness and sleep-tracking apps. Your defining skill is restraint: you know how to make a screen feel calming and legible at 3am without ever using a hard black or a bright glare.

</role>

<reference_data>
Color tokens:
- Screen-wrapping vertical gradient: top #2A2D5A, mid #3B4371, bottom #14152E (never pure black #000000, never pure white as a field)
- Surface 1 #1E2046 (cards), Surface 2 #292C58 (chips, ring track, segmented track), Divider #353974
- The one bright accent: Aqua #4FD1E6, with a slightly brighter Aqua Soft #7FE3F0 reserved for the wave stroke itself
- Secondary interactive: Accent Indigo #6C7BFF (pressed #5563E6), Deep Sleep Indigo #3D4ABF — these two form the primary-button gradient, never a solid fill
- Fixed sleep-stage palette: Awake #FF8FB1, Light Sleep #6C7BFF, Deep Sleep #3D4ABF, REM #4FD1E6, In-Bed/idle #6C70A8
- Text: primary #F2F3FB, secondary (muted lavender) #A6A9D4, tertiary #6C70A8
- Score-banded ring colors: below 50 = #FF8FB1, 50-74 = #6C7BFF, 75-100 = #4FD1E6
- Light "Dawn" mode: canvas #F4F5FC, surface #FFFFFF, divider #E3E5F2

Typeface ladder: Nunito (rounded humanist sans), hero numerals at 900 weight (34pt), section titles 800, body 400 in muted lavender — the contrast between very heavy numerals and very light prose is the entire hierarchy strategy. Eyebrow labels are 12pt/700 uppercase in aqua with 1.4pt tracking.

Corner radius scale: 12pt stage chips/icon tiles, 16pt primary buttons, 20pt hero/graph cards, 28pt bottom-sheet tops, 999pt pills/segmented controls, 50% for the ring and avatars.

Distinctive named patterns to reproduce:
1. Sleep-analysis hypnogram — a full-width card containing a smooth glowing bezier wave (not bars or steps) drawn in the bright aqua stroke over a vertical gradient fill that fades to nothing at the baseline, with small stage-colored event dots and hour-tick x-axis labels.
2. Sleep-quality ring — a circular arc (roughly 92pt), a muted track, and a progress arc whose color is banded by score value, with a big center numeral and a small uppercase sublabel.
3. Smart-alarm card — a horizontal row: a gradient icon tile, a title/subtitle pair, and a large trailing wake-time numeral.
4. Sleep-stage chip — a small pill colored by stage, with contrast-appropriate text color per stage (light text on the darker stages, dark ink on the lighter/brighter ones).

</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Exactly one bright, saturated color exists in the whole palette (the aqua) — every other hue is muted indigo, lavender, or a soft rose/gold used sparingly for stars or streaks; never introduce a second loud color competing for attention.
2. The screen background is always the vertical indigo-to-night gradient, never a flat fill and never pure black — the canvas should feel like it is glowing softly, not glaring.
3. Numerals carry all the emotional weight: hero stats (sleep score, hours slept, wake time) render at 800-900 weight, while every supporting sentence of copy stays at regular 400 weight in the muted lavender secondary color.
4. The sleep-stage color mapping (Awake/Light/Deep/REM) is fixed and reused identically on the hypnogram, chips, and legends — never recolor a stage per-screen.
5. The sleep-quality ring's color is derived from the score band, never a single fixed hue — treat the three-way color shift as a required behavior, not a cosmetic option.
6. Shadows throughout are soft, large-blur, and low-contrast (never a hard black drop shadow); the one exception is the primary button, which gets a colored indigo glow instead of a gray shadow, reinforcing the "light, not shadow" motif.
7. Motion is slow and calming by design — a wave draw-in, a ring sweep, a bar chart's rise from baseline — all easing out over 500-900ms; nothing snaps or bounces.
8. Do not crowd the hypnogram card with other content — it is the visual centerpiece and needs generous surrounding whitespace, consistent with the app's overall breathable, uncluttered spacing.
9. Screens generally have no opaque top navigation bar — a title block (eyebrow + large title + meta line) lives directly in the scrolling content over the gradient.

</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name / product: [e.g., a bedside sleep-tracking companion]

- Screens needed (pick from: nightly sleep report, trends/statistics, smart alarm setup, soundscape/sleep-aid player, sleep journal): [list]
- Smart-alarm feature required?: [yes/no, and wake-window length if yes]
- Light "Dawn" mode required?: [yes/no]
- Platform target (iPhone only / iPhone+iPad / +Watch companion): [fill in]
- Any brand-name substitutions for the aqua accent, if this isn't literally Sleep Cycle: [fill in or "keep as-is"]

</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete SwiftUI Color and Font extension file implementing every token above, ready to paste into a project.
2. Full SwiftUI view code for the sleep-analysis hypnogram card, including the bezier wave path, the gradient fill, the legend, and the stroke draw-in animation.
3. Full SwiftUI view code for the score-banded sleep-quality ring paired with its hero stat block.
4. Full SwiftUI view code for the smart-alarm card and the primary gradient button (with its colored glow shadow).
5. A short written rationale (5-8 bullets) explaining how the requested screens in <the_project> should be composed from these components and in what order.
6. A do/don't checklist (10 items) an engineer can use to sanity-check any new screen against this calm, single-accent system before merging.

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer who specializes in social fitness and route-tracking apps built around map data. Your defining skill is making a map-derived visual (a GPS route) the emotional centerpiece of a screen while keeping every other design decision quiet and neutral around it.

</role>

<reference_data>
Color tokens:
- Light mode canvas: pure white #FFFFFF; Surface Warm #F5F4F2 (search fields, section backgrounds); Surface Cool #F0F0F0 (card dividers/inputs); Divider #E5E5E5
- Dark mode canvas: coal black #0F0F0F (not pure black); Dark Surface 1 #1A1A1A; Dark Surface 2 #262626; Dark Divider #2A2A2A
- The single brand accent: signature Orange #FC4C02 (pressed #D44002), used on the record/CTA button, the active tab, the route polyline, and the filled kudos icon — and nowhere else competes with it
- Map tile colors: warm parchment #E8E5DD (light), deep charcoal #1B1B1B (dark) — never neutral gray tiles
- Ink text: primary #0E0E0E (light) / #F2F2F2 (dark), secondary #666666 (light) / #A0A0A0 (dark)
- Rank/achievement colors: Gold #F5C24A (PR/1st), Silver #C6C6C6 (2nd), Bronze #CD7F32 (3rd)
- Chart overlay colors: pace line blue #3B82F6, elevation fill brown #8B6F47, heart-rate red #E74C3C

Typeface ladder: the system sans (SF Pro Display for titles 20pt+, SF Pro Text for body), with tabular/monospaced-digit figures mandatory on every number — pace, distance, elapsed time, splits, kudos count, follower count. Hero stat numerals on an activity-detail screen run as heavy as 900 weight at 44pt; stat labels are always 11pt uppercase semibold with wide (~0.6pt) tracking.

Corner radius scale: 6pt on the map snapshot itself, 8pt on primary buttons/text fields/most rectangular chrome (deliberately semi-soft, not a full pill), 10pt on search fields, 500pt (full pill) on achievement badges, 50% on avatars and rank chips.

Distinctive named patterns to reproduce:
1. Route polyline rendering — a thick solid-color stroke with a translucent same-hue halo drawn beneath it (so the route reads over a busy map), rounded caps and joins, with distinct start/end marker dots.
2. Activity feed card — avatar+name header, activity title, an optional description, a full-width 16:9 map snapshot with the polyline, a 3-up stat grid (e.g. distance/time/pace) directly below the map, and a kudos+comment row at the bottom; the card itself has no border or shadow — the map photo alone provides visual hierarchy.
3. 3-up stat grid — three equal columns, each an uppercase tracked label over a bold tabular value, with a thin vertical divider between cells in light mode only.
4. Segment/leaderboard row — a circular rank chip (colored gold/silver/bronze for the top three, neutral otherwise), an avatar, stacked name/date, and a stacked time/gap-to-leader on the trailing edge.
5. The record/central-action button — a circle that protrudes slightly above the tab bar, filled in the brand accent, with a colored glow shadow beneath it — the one element in the whole app allowed real elevation.

</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. The single brand accent is the entire chromatic vocabulary for interactive/celebratory moments — never introduce a second saturated brand color; everything else is a careful neutral gradient from white/coal-black through warm grays.
2. Every numeric value on screen (pace, distance, time, splits, follower/kudos counts) must render with tabular/monospaced-digit figures — column alignment in any stats table depends on it and must never be allowed to drift to proportional digits.
3. The route polyline is never drawn as a bare stroke — it always carries a translucent halo of the same hue beneath it, because a bare accent-colored line disappears against a busy street map.
4. The 3-up stat grid is the universal pattern for summarizing an activity — never collapse it into a plain list or bullet points; it must always present exactly three (or occasionally four, on larger devices) evenly divided columns.
5. Cards are flat by default — no border, no drop shadow — because the map snapshot itself is expected to carry all the visual weight and separation; reserve real elevation (a colored glow shadow) for exactly one element: the primary record/action button.
6. Stat labels are always uppercase, semibold, and tracked wide (~0.6pt) — this is the app's consistent "data voice" and should never downshift to sentence case or a lighter weight.
7. Achievement/rank colors (gold/silver/bronze) are fixed hex values distinct from any system-default yellow — never substitute a generic gold or a saturated system yellow.
8. Dark mode uses a slightly warm coal black rather than a pure neutral or pure black — this keeps the accent-colored polyline and glow shadows reading vividly rather than washing out.
9. Haptic and motion weight should be proportional to stakes: the heaviest haptic in the app is reserved for the central record/start action; a celebratory tap-and-bounce animation (with a brief particle burst) is reserved for the social kudos/approval gesture.

</house_rules>

<the_project>

- Screens needed (pick from: activity feed, activity detail, segment/leaderboard, record/start flow, profile grid, groups/clubs): [list]

- Achievement/PR system required?: [yes/no]
- Platform target (iPhone only / iPhone+iPad): [fill in]
- Any brand-name substitutions for the orange accent, if this isn't literally Strava: [fill in or "keep as-is"]

</the_project>

2. Full SwiftUI view code for the activity feed card, including the map snapshot placeholder, the polyline-with-halo rendering, the 3-up stat grid, and the kudos row with its tap animation.

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer who specializes in utilitarian, data-dense logging tools for strength training. Your defining skill is stripping away every decorative impulse so a lifter can log a set with two taps between heavy sets, without the interface ever getting in the way.

</role>

<reference_data>
Color tokens (true neutral grey, never blue-tinted):
- Canvas #1A1A1A (flat near-black, the launch surface), Card Surface #242424, Input Surface #2E2E2E (editable cells, stat pills, search field), Surface 3 #383838 (thumbnails, pressed rows), Divider #333333
- The single accent: Strong Blue #2F80ED (pressed #2566C0, soft tint fill #16263D at ~14-22% opacity) — used on the Finish button, active tab, exercise-name text/links, and the rest-timer fill; there is no second brand hue
- Text: primary (near-white) #F5F5F5, secondary #9A9A9A, tertiary #636363
- Semantic: Set-Done Green #27AE60 (row fill at ~18% opacity when a set is checked off), PR Amber #F2C94C (personal-record flag), Destructive Red #EB5757, Warning/Warm-up Orange #F2994A
- Light-mode variants: canvas #F2F2F2, card #FFFFFF, input #EBEBEB, divider #DDDDDD (the accent blue and semantic colors stay identical in both modes)

Typeface ladder: a single humanist sans (no alternate faces) with tabular figures (`tnum`) applied to literally every number on screen — set weight, reps, set index, volume total, estimated 1RM, and any timer — so the set table's columns never reflow as a digit count changes. Sizes: screen title 32/800, workout title 26/800, exercise name 18/700 (always rendered in the accent blue, doubling as a tap-to-replace affordance), metric/timer readouts 17/700 tabular, set-table cell values 15/700 tabular, column labels 11/700 uppercase.

Corner radius scale: 7pt on set cells and stat pills, 8pt on buttons/segmented controls/the rest-timer bar, 14pt on exercise cards and history rows, 20pt on bottom sheets and the plate calculator.

Distinctive named patterns to reproduce:
1. Set-log table row — a compact grid of set-index, a 'previous session' hint value, two editable numeric cells (weight, reps), and a checkbox; checking the box fills the row's cells with a translucent green tint and a solid checkmark, and auto-starts the rest timer.
2. Slim rest-timer bar — a thin horizontal progress bar (not a ring or dial) that depletes linearly over the configured rest duration, with plus/minus adjustment controls and a chime + haptic at zero.
3. Exercise card — a flat, borderless card (depth comes purely from the surface-color step up from canvas, never a border or shadow) with a thumbnail, the exercise name in the accent color, an optional note, the set table, and a full-width tonal "add set" footer row.
4. PR flag — a small inline chip in the amber semantic color that appears the moment a logged set beats a stored personal record, with a brief pulse and haptic.
5. Stat-pill row — three small pills (e.g. time, volume, set count) sitting directly under the workout title, each a muted label plus a bold tabular accent-colored value.

</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Every number on screen — weight, reps, set index, volume, estimated 1RM, timer — is rendered with tabular/monospaced figures; a proportional-figure number anywhere in a table is a defect, since it will visibly reflow column widths as digits change.
2. There is exactly one brand accent color; do not introduce a second blue, a secondary hue, or a gradient brand treatment anywhere — the restraint itself is the personality.
3. Exercise cards are flat and borderless by design — depth is conveyed only by the surface-color step (canvas to card to input-surface), never by adding a border or a drop shadow to a card; this is a deliberate, load-bearing rule, not an oversight.
4. A "previous performance" reference value must appear inline on every loggable set row — this is the core value proposition of the whole product and must never be hidden behind a tap or a secondary screen.
5. Completing a set fills that row's cells with a translucent version of the semantic "done" color and immediately starts a rest-timer countdown — logging and resting are one continuous interaction, not two separate steps.
6. The canvas and all surface tiers are true neutral grey, never tinted toward the brand blue or any other hue — this "instrument panel" neutrality is what makes the single accent color pop when it does appear.
7. Celebratory moments (personal records) are restrained: a colored flag chip, a brief pulse, and a soft haptic — never confetti, never a full-screen takeover.
8. Motion throughout is fast and functional (roughly 120-300ms), never springy or playful — tab switching in particular should feel instantaneous with no cross-fade, reinforcing that this tool must never slow a lifter down mid-session.
9. Micro-labels (column headers, tab labels, the PR flag) are the only place uppercase styling is used — body copy, titles, and exercise names are always sentence case or title case.

</house_rules>

<the_project>

- Screens needed (pick from: active workout log, exercise library, history/calendar, body measurements/charts, plate calculator, post-workout summary): [list]
- Set-type tagging needed (warm-up/drop/failure sets)?: [yes/no]
- Rest-timer default duration and adjustability: [fill in]
- Platform target (iPhone only / iPhone+iPad): [fill in]
- Any brand-name substitutions for the blue accent, if this isn't literally Strong: [fill in or "keep as-is"]

</the_project>

2. Full SwiftUI view code for the set-log table row, including the editable weight/reps cells, the checkbox fill-on-complete behavior, and the previous-value hint.
3. Full SwiftUI view code for the exercise card (header, set table, add-set footer) and the slim rest-timer bar with its ±adjustment controls.
4. Full SwiftUI view code for the PR flag chip and the stat-pill row.

Color tokens (dark-canvas-only — there is no light mode):
- Canvas #0A0A0A (near-black, every screen), Surface 1 #1C1C1E (cards, sheets, tab bar), Surface 2 #2A2A2A (chips, inputs, sliders), Surface 3 #3A3A3A (highest elevation), Divider/Hairline #252525
- Signature strain accent: neon Strain Green #00FF7B (bright variant #67E26B, dim/disabled #005F2F) — the primary CTA color and active-tab tint
- Recovery spectrum (interpolates continuously by score, in 1% increments): Recovery Red #FF0026 (0-33%), Recovery Yellow #FFDE00 (34-66%), Recovery Green #16EC06 (67-100%)
- Sleep accent family: Sleep Blue #0093E7 (bright #4FB8FF), plus stage colors REM Purple #9C4DFF, Deep Sleep Indigo #3D3DFF, Light Sleep Cyan #3DD9FF
- Text: bright white #FFFFFF (reserved for hero numerals only), soft white #F5F5F7 (body), gray-400 #A1A1AA (secondary/captions), gray-600 #5F5F65 (tertiary/disabled)
- Distinct semantic set (deliberately NOT reusing the recovery ramp): Alert Red #FF453A, Warning Amber #FFAA00, Info Blue #0A84FF, Success Green #30D158, Premium Gold #D4AF37

Typeface ladder: a flat, mechanically-engineered instrumentation-style sans, with hero numerals scaling up to 76pt at weight 800 for the top-line recovery percentage and 56pt for the strain score — both with tight negative tracking. All-caps with wide letter-spacing (0.6-1.6pt) is the dominant header treatment for section labels, button labels, tab labels, and meta tags; body copy stays sentence case. Every metric value uses tabular/monospaced figures without exception.

Corner radius scale: 4pt on primary buttons and badges (deliberately almost-square, not a pill), 8pt on inputs/search, 12pt on metric and coaching cards, 16pt on hero containers, 24pt on bottom-sheet tops, 500pt reserved only for rare chip pills, 50% for the recovery ring, activity icons, and day-switcher dots.

Distinctive named patterns to reproduce:
1. Recovery ring — a large circular gauge, open at the top with a small gap between the stroke's start and end, whose fill color interpolates continuously red-to-yellow-to-green based on the live score, with a giant tabular percentage in the center.
2. Strain bar — a thick horizontal bar filled with a green gradient, tick marks at named strain thresholds, and a small circular marker that slides along it in real time as strain accumulates.
3. Metric card — a compact ring or hero number paired with a caps label, plus a row of supplementary tabular metrics beneath it, defined entirely by a hairline border rather than any shadow.
4. Sleep-stage stacked bar — a single horizontal bar segmented by sleep stage in time order, with an hourly time axis beneath it and a tappable callout per segment.
5. Day-switcher strip — a horizontal row of day chips where the selected day is a solid filled circle in the strain accent and the others are outlined.

</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. There is no light mode anywhere in this system — every screen, without exception, renders on the near-black canvas; do not generate a light variant even if asked for one casually.
2. The recovery ring's fill color is never a fixed hue — it must always interpolate continuously along the red-yellow-green spectrum based on the live score value, changing in fine (roughly 1%) increments rather than snapping between three discrete colors.
3. All-caps with wide letter-spacing is mandatory on every section header, button label, tab label, and meta tag; sentence-case body text is the only place normal casing appears — breaking this rule anywhere undermines the instrument-panel identity.
4. Every metric value (heart-rate variability, resting heart rate, strain, sleep duration, any percentage) renders with tabular/monospaced figures with zero exceptions, including compound values like a duration with mixed units.
5. Primary buttons use an almost-square 4pt corner radius, never a pill or a softly-rounded rectangle — this radius choice is as load-bearing to the brand identity as the color palette.
6. Elevation is conveyed by a 1pt hairline border plus, for genuinely live/active elements only, a soft neon glow — never by a conventional neutral drop shadow, since the canvas is already darker than most shadows would read against.
7. The strain-green accent is reserved for strain and general primary actions only; it must never be reused to represent recovery, sleep, or any other metric family, each of which has its own dedicated color.
8. The bottom navigation is exactly four tabs; do not add a fifth without being explicitly asked to restructure the whole navigation model.
9. Negative space between major sections is generous and deliberate (very wide vertical gaps) — the dark canvas and the numbers are meant to feel like they have room to "breathe," not be packed edge-to-edge.

</house_rules>

description: Recreates the videogame-meets-fitness aesthetic of an indoor cycling/virtual-world app — translucent glass overlays floating over a 3D scene, a condensed display face for oversized ride metrics, and a dual off-ride dark app shell as paste-ready SwiftUI.

whatYouGet: A SwiftUI token file covering both the in-ride glassmorphic overlay system and the off-ride dark app shell, with a fixed semantic color mapping for ride metrics
The signature rider HUD (glass metric tiles), route banner, and power-up game-mechanic tile built out in SwiftUI with their real update/collect animations

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer who specializes in game-like heads-up-display interfaces layered over a live 3D rendered scene, for indoor training and virtual-world fitness apps. Your defining skill is designing chrome that must remain legible from two metres away on a device propped in front of a trainer, without ever visually smothering the world behind it.

</role>

<reference_data>
Color tokens:
- Brand action color: Orange #FC6719 (pressed #D9530E, soft tint #3A2110 at ~12-20% opacity) — used for the start-ride CTA, default rider jersey, route-progress fill, and an armed game power-up
- Fixed ride-metric semantic colors (do not remap): Power #FC6719 (shares brand orange, since power is the hero metric), Cadence #E8C547 (warm yellow), Heart-Rate #F0413E (red), W/kg & Effort #2BD4D9 (cyan), Speed/Distance/Time #FFFFFF (neutral)
- Glass overlay surfaces (used only in-ride, over the 3D world): Glass Panel rgba(12,12,12,0.60) with an 8pt blur for HUD tiles/banners, Glass Panel Heavy rgba(15,15,15,0.80) with a 12-20pt blur for the action bar/modals, a 1pt rgba(255,255,255,0.10) hairline stroke on all glass
- Off-ride app-shell surfaces (solid, conventional dark UI): App Canvas #161616, Card Surface #1F1F1F, Surface 2/3 #2A2A2A/#353535, Divider #303030
- Text: primary pure white #FFFFFF (max contrast against both the world and dark shell), secondary #A8AAAD, tertiary #6C6E72
- Achievement/success color: Green #57C84D, distinct from the brand orange

Typeface ladder: a two-face system — a tall condensed display face for every large number, screen title, route name, and button label (chosen because condensed glyphs pack maximum legibility into small glass tiles at a distance), and a standard humanist sans for body copy, list rows, and captions where small-size readability matters more than visual punch. HUD metric values run 28-34pt at weight 800 with tabular figures; unit labels are 11pt/700 uppercase. Titles and button labels are frequently uppercase (game energy); body text stays sentence case.

Corner radius scale: 10pt on buttons, glass buttons, the power-up tile, and search fields; 12pt on HUD tiles, the route banner, and off-ride cards; 20pt on bottom sheets; 500pt on "join"/category pills; 50% on avatars and mini-map dots; 0pt for the full-bleed world itself and the elevation-profile strip edges.

Distinctive named patterns to reproduce:
1. Rider HUD — a row of 3-5 glass metric tiles anchored near the bottom of a full-bleed 3D scene, each tile showing one metric in its fixed semantic color at a large tabular size with a small uppercase unit label beneath.
2. Route banner — a translucent strip anchored at the top clearing the notch/Dynamic Island, showing the route name, a distance/lap sub-line, and a thin orange progress bar beneath it.
3. Power-up tile — a small square game-ability control: translucent glass when unarmed, solid brand-orange with a glyph when armed, with a scale-pop-and-glow animation on collection.
4. In-ride action bar — a heavy-glass bottom bar hosting game controls (not page navigation) such as an emote/action button, the power-up, workout view, rider list, and menu.
5. Off-ride route card — a conventional solid dark card with a world thumbnail, an elevation sparkline in the brand orange, and a stats row — used only outside an active ride.

</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. During an active ride, the 3D world is always full-bleed and is treated as the actual canvas — never place an opaque background behind any in-ride panel; every in-ride surface must be translucent glass so the scene remains visible through it.
2. The metric-to-color mapping (power/cadence/heart-rate/effort) is fixed and must never be remapped or restyled per screen — riders are expected to recognize a metric by its color alone, the same way a real cockpit's gauges are colored consistently.
3. HUD numerals never shrink to fit more chrome — legibility from roughly two metres away is a hard constraint that overrides any layout-density concern; if tiles don't fit, reduce the tile count before reducing the type size.
4. Every ride metric renders with tabular/monospaced figures, and value changes should be interpolated smoothly over a short duration rather than snapping instantly, so the HUD never visibly "jumps" as a number updates.
5. In-ride glass panels never receive a conventional drop shadow — separation from the 3D scene comes only from translucency, blur, and a thin light-colored hairline stroke; a drop shadow on glass reads as visually pasted onto the world.
6. The two typefaces are never mixed within a single text element — the condensed display face is reserved for numbers/titles/buttons, and the standard sans is reserved for body/list/caption text.
7. Off-ride screens (menus, route picker, profile, workout library) fall back entirely to the solid, conventional dark app-shell palette — glass and translucency are exclusively an in-ride treatment and must not appear in the off-ride shell.
8. The bottom bar shown during an active ride is a set of game controls, not page navigation, and must be visually and behaviorally distinct from the off-ride app-shell tab bar.
9. Achievement and celebration moments use the dedicated green success color plus a brief orange accent flourish — never reuse the brand orange alone to signal "success," since orange's primary job is the brand action/power metric.

</house_rules>
